summary: Multiple unauthorized device registration attempts detected after targeted phishing email
description: Issue summary: Multiple failed device registration attempts using the mobile-enroll API were observed beginning 2026-03-12 08:12 UTC. Attempts originated from IPs that correlate with a targeted spearphishing email campaign sent to a subset of employees earlier the same morning. Impact: Potential credential reuse or intercepted cookies could allow attacker to pair devices to accounts; no confirmed successful enrollments as of this update. Environment: production (us-east), mobile-enroll-v2 service behind SSO. Initial detection: Automated anomaly rule in SIEM (enrollment-fail-rate spike) alerted on 2026-03-12 08:15 UTC. The alert included multiple account IDs with overlapping device fingerprints and user-agent strings resembling a headless browser. Steps to reproduce (observed attack pattern): 1) Phishing email contains link to a spoofed device onboarding flow. 2) Victim clicks link, authenticates via SSO because session cookie persisted. 3) Attack orchestration attempts automated device enrollment calls using stolen session/token. 4) Enrollment API returns 401/403 or triggers MFA for some accounts. Observed artifacts: IPs from Eastern Europe, high rate of repeated device IDs, user-agents: "Mozilla/5.0 (HeadlessChrome)" variants, repeated 401/429/403 responses in logs. First response: Security triage isolated impacted account list, forced session revocation for accounts with anomalous enroll attempts, and temporarily throttled mobile-enroll-v2 endpoint for non-interactive clients.
steps_to_reproduce: Receive targeted spearphish email with onboarding link (internal test copy used)
Follow link while authenticated to SSO to trigger enroll flow
Automate POST /api/mobile-enroll/v2 with stolen session cookie and varied device_id headers
Observe repeated 401/403 and increased enroll-failure metric in SIEM
logs: Splunk search: index=prod enroll_api status IN (401,403,429) earliest=2026-03-12:08:00 latest=2026-03-12:09:30 | stats count by src_ip, user_agent, account_id
Sample log line: 2026-03-12T08:18:03Z mobile-enroll-v2 WARN account=alice.redwood src_ip=45.79.23.18 ua="HeadlessChrome/97.0" result=401 device_id=dev_f7c3ab
comments: 2026-03-12 08:25 - Maya Chen: Raised after SIEM alert. Initial account list attached to ticket. Marking P1 due to potential account compromise.

2026-03-12 08:40 - Ethan Rodriguez: Revoked SSO sessions for 12 accounts with >5 failed enroll attempts. Rate-limited mobile-enroll-v2 for non-browser UA strings. Notified Platform on throttling impact.
2026-03-12 09:05 - Priya Malhotra (SRE): Confirmed spike correlates with outbound email campaign (ID: MAIL-20260312-07). Added temporary WAF rule to block identified IP range.

2026-03-13 11:20 - Security Ops (L. Ortiz): No successful device binding observed. MFA challenge triggered for 3 accounts where device pairing almost succeeded. Requested expanded log retention for enroll API for 7 days.
2026-03-14 07:50 - Legal (G. Alvarez): Requested list of affected employees and timeline for notification; paused until we confirm successful enrollments.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Phishing link proxied to a cloned onboarding site that initiates enroll API calls using the victim's session cookie. Evidence: referrer headers in some POSTs match onboarding flow, and cookies used appear valid for those sessions.
Hypothesis 2: Credential stuffing not primary driver — attempts clustered shortly after mailing window and from small set of IPs. Rate-limiting patterns suggest automated orchestration.

Confirmed: No device records were added to account device tables for affected accounts as of 2026-03-14 06:00 UTC. All enroll requests for accounts that would have bypassed MFA were blocked due to progressive risk checks.
Logs show identical device_id hashes across multiple accounts — indicates either attacker reusing device payload or compromised onboarding client library.
SAML assertion replay was considered; SAML logs show valid SSO flows but no duplicate assertion IDs beyond normal noise.
resolution: Mitigation performed: 1) Revoked active SSO sessions for all accounts in the impacted cohort and forced password resets for accounts with successful MFA bypass attempts. 2) Temporary WAF and IP block for suspicious IP ranges. 3) Throttled mobile-enroll-v2 for non-standard user-agents and added stricter device_id entropy checks. 4) Increased enroll API logging and extended retention to 14 days for post-incident analysis. 5) Rolled out a quick configuration change to require step-up MFA for any device enrollment requests from new device fingerprints. Follow-up actions: full postmortem if evidence of successful enrollments emerges; update phishing training for recipients, add automation to detect identical device_id reuse across accounts, and schedule a security review of the onboarding client library. Notified HR/Legal for potential user notification pending confirmation of compromise.
next_steps: Complete forensics on increased log retention window and export full enroll API request payloads for 2026-03-12 07:45 - 09:30 UTC
Coordinate with Email Ops to verify exact recipient list for MAIL-20260312-07 and revoke/sanitise any follow-up emails
Implement permanent device enrollment risk checks (entropy + UA heuristics) in mobile-enroll-v2 by 2026-03-21
Create automated alert for identical device_id across >=3 distinct account_ids
estimated_impact: Potential: ~120 employees received the phishing email; 18 accounts showed anomalous enroll traffic; 0 confirmed successful device enrollments to date. Operational impact: brief friction for legitimate mobile enrollments in us-east during throttling window.
